newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Music industry to demand EU policy at hearing.
newsitem.headline: Music industry to demand EU policy at hearing.

text.p: Europe's multi-billion-dollar music industry gathers in Brussels on Wednesday for an all-day session to demand a European Union policy on pop music.

The hearing, organised by Greek singer turned Member of the European Parliament Nana Mouskouri, will tackle the piracy, copyright, trade and cultural issues seen as central to the $24 billion sector's prospects.

Although the EU has a well-established policy to help its struggling film industry, the music sector complains the European Commission has not put forward a policy to address problems holding back the successful music industry.
"Music is a major influence and a huge motivating force with significant impact and it's about time the Commission became interested in music," Mouskouri said in a statement.
She said she would push for an EU move to reduce value added tax on sound recordings.
"VAT has to be the first thing we have to consider and I hope it will be harmonised downwards. I don't think the industry should suffer from these taxes," she said.

The industry argues that sound recordings should be treated as cultural goods rather than commercial objects and receive the same zero VAT-rating enjoyed by books. But such a move would have to be agreed unanimously by EU governments.

The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), which will send top executives from major labels like PolyGram and Virgin France, said on Tuesday it will put the emphasis on the need for EU action against rampant piracy which saps $2 billion a year in profits.
A spokesman said it would also urge a more watertight legal framework for copyright in the developing information society and a fair VAT system for recordings.
The IFPI said in a statement Europe was the record industry's largest market worth $13 billion per year.
"European artists are predominant across the continent and the industry employs more than 300,000 people in Europe," it said.
"The record industry's delegation will call on the EU for strong policies that reflect the industry's growing economic and cultural importance in Europe."
